subject: [HyperBurst] Sudden latency + 5xx spike — need exec bridge/CEO awareness
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <ops@hyperburst.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@hyperburst.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for HyperBurst prod (US-WEST-2)

Jonas —

We’re seeing a sustained latency increase and an uptick in 5xx errors starting ~08:45 PDT across our US-WEST-2 traffic. 99th percentile latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s and error rate climbed to 3.8% for the past 20 minutes. Throughput is slightly down as retries are amplifying.

This is impacting several of our high-QPS routes (search and realtime-suggestions). We’ve been following the Runbook steps but the spike persists after a cache flush. Can you confirm whether you’re seeing regional issues on Redwood’s side and whether a cross-region divert is available? We need a decision ASAP — toward a traffic swap or canary fallback.

Attached: hyperburst_kpis_0900.png (image/png, 240KB)

—Alex
Ops — HyperBurst Inc.
ops@hyperburst.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for HyperBurst prod (US-WEST-2)

Forwarding HyperBurst alert — they’re seeing a sharp P99/5xx spike in US-WEST-2 and have tried the standard runbook (cache flush, scale up, restart inference pool) without stabilization.

Quick ask: can infra confirm whether any AZ-level degraded hardware or scheduled maintenance aligns with their window? If not, recommend we propose an immediate cross-region steer to US-EAST-1 as a short-term mitigation and open an exec bridge if this becomes a broader outage. I’m available to start a bridge.

Jonas
Platform AM — Redwood Inference

On 2027-03-02 09:12 AM, Alex Mercer wrote:
> Jonas —
>
> We’re seeing a sustained latency increase ...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for HyperBurst prod (US-WEST-2)

Jonas —

Infra confirms a partial throttle on one of the inference pools in US-WEST-2; a noisy host degraded KV cache hit rates for certain LLM shapes and caused amplification. We isolated the host at 09:48 and started rebalancing, but recovery has been slow because the affected model (open-vanguard-7b) has heavy prefix cache reliance.

Recommendation (short):
- Immediate: Propose a regional diversion to US-EAST-1 for the affected routes (search, suggestions). Can perform 5–10% gradual shift in 3 steps to validate.
- Parallel: Trigger a pool drain and restart for the noisy hosts (in progress).
- Notify: Exec bridge if HyperBurst wants leadership engaged or if diversion needs approval beyond the standard steering.

I’ve prepared a one-pager for leadership summarizing impact and cost/latency tradeoffs (see attached).

—Marissa
Sr. Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: exec_onepager_hyperburst.pdf (application/pdf, 450KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike for HyperBurst prod (US-WEST-2) — CEO awareness

Team —

Thanks for the quick triage. Given HyperBurst’s SLA profile and the visible customer impact, please escalate to an exec bridge and include the following in the brief: 1) observed metrics (P50/P95/P99, error %, QPS delta), 2) mitigation options (gradual region shift vs. model variant fallback), 3) estimated customer impact window and cost delta for cross-region steer, 4) ask for CEO approval to proceed with a full region divert if metrics don’t stabilize in 30 minutes.

Jonas: open the incident bridge and invite HyperBurst. Sean: can you draft the one-slide exec summary and include a recommended play (I favor controlled divert + short-term credits if customer asks)? Marissa: continue backend remedial work and give an ETA for pool recovery.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <ops@hyperburst.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@hyperburst.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: EXEC BRIDGE BRIEF: HyperBurst US-WEST-2 latency + 5xx surge (recommended action)

Team / HyperBurst —

Bridge established: https://app.redwood.com/incidents/HYP-2027-03-02

Summary (120m window):
- Impact: P99 latency increased to ~1.2s, error rate peaked at 3.8%, ~18% effective QPS reduction due to client retries.
- Root cause (interim): Noisy inference host + KV cache hit drop during heavy open-vanguard-7b requests in US-WEST-2. Host isolated; drain underway.
- Recommended immediate action: Controlled cross-region diversion of affected routes to US-EAST-1 with a 3-step 10% -> 30% -> 60% shift over 12 minutes, monitor application-level errors. If error rate drops below 0.5% at 60% shift, continue full migration.
- Risk/Cost: Additional inter-region egress and slightly higher latency on some queries (~+40–80ms at 60% traffic). Estimated incremental cost for 3 hours: ~$2.5K for HyperBurst (can apply support credit if requested).
- Ask for CEO-level signoff window: 30 minutes to approve full divert if stabilization criteria are not met.

Attachments: exec_onepager_hyperburst.pdf, hyperburst_kpis_0900.png

Alex/Laura — can you confirm whether you want to accept the diversion now or prefer Redwood to continue pool-only remediation?

—Sean Gallagher
Head of Escalations — Redwood Inference
Attachment: exec_onepager_hyperburst.pdf
